example.title: Identifying the Magnitude of a Vector From a Diagram

question.text: Given the diagram above, where $|\mathbf{a}|=3\sqrt{2}$ and $|\mathbf{b}|=6$, find the value of $|\mathbf{a+b}|.$
question.explanation:
We use the triangle law for adding the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$

Using the law of cosines, we obtain:

\begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={\mathbf{|a|}}^2+{\mathbf{|b|}}^2-2\mathbf{|a||b|}\cos ({135}^\circ) \\[5pt] &=\left(3\sqrt{2}\right)^2+{6}^2-2 \cdot 3\sqrt{2} \cdot 6 \cdot \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\[5pt] &=18+36+36 \\[5pt] &=90 \end{align*}

Hence, $|\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{90}=3\sqrt{10}.$
